overall: Violation found where the Board discussed an anticipated 146 Plymouth Street project not listed on the August 16 notice; the second allegation was declined, and only immediate and future compliance was ordered.

allegations.summary: Board discussed the 146 Plymouth Street project at its August 16 meeting though the topic was anticipated but not listed on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the topic of the project at 146 Plymouth Street was anticipated but not included on the meeting notice, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing the topic during its August 16 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed having members attend private meetings with the project applicant and abutters.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern the substance of a public body’s discussions, and the complaint does not allege that a quorum of the Board in fact attended a private meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
